result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a continuous sidewalk along a residential row-house street, but lacks any dedicated crossing infrastructure. Parked vehicles along the curb create significant sightline obstructions, which is the primary safety concern for pedestrians in this area.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block the visibility of pedestrians, especially children, who might attempt to cross the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line where the red car is parked.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or potential crossing points to improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install 'continental' style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is car-oriented with a wide roadway and a complete lack of marked crossings or traffic control devices at the intersection. While sidewalks are present, the design prioritizes vehicle throughput and offers little protection or visibility for people walking.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks marked crosswalks, leaving pedestrians without a designated or protected space to cross the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: The excessive width of the travel lanes and lack of traffic calming may encourage high vehicle speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway stretching into the distance

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings to clearly delineate pedestrian paths and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Add signage to warn drivers of potential pedestrian activity at the intersection.

result.summary: The environment is a residential area with row houses and a wide asphalt roadway. While sidewalks are present, the lack of marked crossings on the main road and the wide street width likely encourage higher vehicle speeds, creating a hostile environment for pedestrians crossing the primary thoroughfare.

hazards.name: Wide roadway
hazards.description: The width of the main road encourages higher vehicle speeds and increases pedestrian exposure time.

hazards.name: Lack of main road crossing
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs for crossing the primary street.

hazards.name: Sight line obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on the side street may obstruct sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style markings across the main road to increase driver awareness and define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Reduce crossing distance and improve sight lines by extending the sidewalk at the intersection corners.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential zone.

result.summary: The image shows a wide residential street with sidewalks but lacks marked pedestrian crossings across the primary roadway. Faded pavement markings and parked vehicles near the intersection create potential visibility and safety issues for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corner may block the view between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
